questions.prompt: fetch_url has timeoutMs 5000 and the server answers after 8 seconds. What does the model receive, and when?
options: A timeout error, after 5 seconds, because fetch received the deadline signal
Nothing, because the call is dropped
questions.explanation: The wrapper put a 5000 ms deadline on the signal that fetch watches. fetch rejects at 5 seconds, and the wrapper replaces the error with the timeout message.

questions.prompt: A tool body with timeoutMs 5000 runs a loop that never checks its signal and ends after 60 seconds. What happens?
options: The wrapper kills the loop at 5 seconds
The call fails before it starts
The wrapper waits until the loop ends, because the timeout depends on the body watching its signal
questions.explanation: The timeout is cooperative. A wrapper in the same process can abort a signal but cannot stop code that never reads it.

questions.prompt: Why does the timeout wrapper put the old signal back in a finally block?
options: So later code never sees this plugin's deadline signal
So the body can run a second time
Because AbortSignal.timeout can only be used once
questions.explanation: The deadline belongs to the wrapper. Restoring the caller's own signal means listeners that run afterwards do not see a signal that this plugin aborted.
